title: Polynesian settlement of East Polynesia
summary: Polynesian voyagers from the Samoa and Tonga area settled the Society Islands around AD 1025-1120, then spread within about a century to the remaining islands, including Hawaii, Rapa Nui and New Zealand. A 2011 study of high-precision radiocarbon dates shortened earlier chronologies by several centuries.

uncertainty.note: Years are calendar years AD, taking midpoints of the ranges in Wilmshurst et al. 2011: Society Islands ~1025-1120; Rapa Nui ~1200-1253; Hawaii ~1219-1266; New Zealand ~1230-1282. Gambier is dated more broadly (~1108-1275). Earlier chronologies placed settlement from AD 300-600 in the Marquesas; this study rejects those for unreliable samples, and the debate is continuing. The waypoints show arrival dates for island groups in order, not a single voyage; the Marquesas and other groups are omitted.

where.modern_name: Society Islands, French Polynesia (first waypoint; archipelago centroid)
where.historical_name: Central East Polynesia before European contact; no recorded place names

waypoints.label: Society Islands, French Polynesia: earliest dated colonization in East Polynesia. Point is the archipelago centroid.
Rapa Nui (Easter Island): island colonization, short chronology confirmed.
Hawaii: archipelago colonization; the point is Hawaii island, the largest, but the study dates the archipelago.
New Zealand (Aotearoa): colonization. Point is the national centroid; the study dates the island group.

importance.justification: The last major settlement of habitable land by humans, completed by deliberate ocean voyaging.

related.because: East Polynesians descend from Lapita-era settlers of West Polynesia.

reviewer_note: Least sure: no dated West Polynesian starting waypoint is included (Wilmshurst says only that Polynesians dispersed from the Samoa-Tonga area); the waypoints are island-group arrival dates in order, not one voyage; Hawaii and New Zealand points are centroids; the short chronology is the current mainstream view but older longer chronologies still appear in the literature.

beats.caption: Voyagers settle the Society Islands, the earliest dated landfall in East Polynesia, about four centuries later than once assumed.
After a pause of 70-265 years, settlers reach Rapa Nui, Hawaii and New Zealand within roughly a century.
With New Zealand settled, Polynesians occupy almost every habitable island group across the Pacific, a triangle from Hawaii to Rapa Nui to New Zealand.
